entries.name: receiver-kind-encode_nbits_global_control-wrapped-accept#0
entries.description: `sigmaProp(row 1 == control)`. `Global.encodeNbits(BigInt 1)` with the receiver `Global` — the CONTROL. Evaluates to `16842752L` at cost 39. The CONTROL of the controls: both sides are the well-formed call, so it parses AND reduces to `SigmaProp(true)` at cost 96 — the one of the seven whose box can be spent.

entries.name: receiver-kind-encode_nbits_int_receiver-wrapped-accept#1
entries.description: `sigmaProp(row 2 == control)`. `encodeNbits` with the receiver an `Int` CONSTANT. Parses — the serializer checks no receiver — and the reflective invoke then refuses it. **SEPARATING:** an implementation whose evaluator never reads its receiver returns the control's value instead. A CONTROL, not evidence: the wrong receiver is refused at EVAL and nowhere earlier, so this tree is a legal script that parses and round-trips verbatim on every implementation. It is here to license the eval and transaction rows — if it ever goes red, their reds stop meaning what they say.
